WB_Overview: Enables RNA polymerase II-specific DNA-binding transcription factor binding activity; scaffold protein binding activity; and transcription coactivator activity. Involved in several processes, including cell fate commitment involved in formation of primary germ layer; gonad development; and regulation of gene expression. Located in several cellular components, including cell cortex; kinetochore; and pericentriolar material. Expressed in several structures, including ABplpapaap; ABprpapaap; Z1.aa; posterior distal tip cell; and tail hypodermis.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable signaling receptor complex adaptor activity. WB_Overview: Predicted to enable clathrin binding activity. Involved in receptor-mediated endocytosis. Predicted to be located in intracellular membrane-bounded organelle and vesicle. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in Parkinson's disease 19A. Is an ortholog of human DNAJC6 (DnaJ heat shock protein family (Hsp40) member C6).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: The dnj-25 (Ce-auxilin) gene is required in vivo for clathrin-mediated endocytosis and for normal development.
Narrative: An upstream variant could reduce expression of DNJ-25 (auxilin), impairing endocytic trafficking of cell-surface receptors and thereby altering asymmetric signalling required for AMso-to-MCM fate decisions [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=MODIFIER; QUAL=23.7; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="dnj-25 required for clathrin-mediated endocytosis."]
rationale: DNJ-25 (auxilin) is required for clathrin-mediated endocytosis and could alter membrane/cortical receptor dynamics that specify asymmetric divisions.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable dynein light intermediate chain binding activity and small GTPase binding activity. Predicted to be involved in cilium assembly. Predicted to be located in ciliary basal body and cytoplasm. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in oculopharyngodistal myopathy 4. Is an ortholog of human RILPL1 (Rab interacting lysosomal protein like 1).
Narrative: An upstream variant in rilp-1 may alter intracellular trafficking via dynein interactions; mis-trafficking of polarity factors or fate determinants could disrupt asymmetric AMso division and prevent MCM neuron birth [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=MODIFIER; QUAL=17.7; WB_Overview="Predicted to enable dynein light intermediate chain binding activity."].
rationale: RILP-1 binds dynein/light intermediate chains and small GTPases and participates in cilium/transport processes that can affect intracellular trafficking of polarity determinants.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable GTPase activator activity. Predicted to be involved in small GTPase-mediated signal transduction. Predicted to be located in cytoplasm and plasma membrane. Is an ortholog of human ARHGAP12 (Rho GTPase activating protein 12).
Narrative: A TAG-325 missense could modify Rho GTPase regulation at the cortex, impairing cytoskeletal polarization and correct asymmetric partitioning in AMso divisions so that both daughters become glia instead of producing an MCM neuron [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=32.2; WB_Overview="Predicted to enable GTPase activator activity."].
rationale: TAG-325 is predicted to be a Rho GTPase-activating protein, and Rho GTPase signaling is central to cell polarity and asymmetric division decisions.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable calcium ion binding activity. Predicted to be involved in cell-cell adhesion. Predicted to be located in membrane. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in Van Maldergem syndrome 1 and mitral valve prolapse. Is an ortholog of human DCHS1 (dachsous cadherin-related 1).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: cdh-1 encodes a cadherin that is similar, in the extracellular domain, to the Drosophila cadherin Dachsous (Ds); although the precise role of cdh-1 in C. elegans development and/or behavior is not yet known, loss of cdh-1 activity via RNAi using the hypersensitive rrf-3 strain can result in locomotion and growth defects, as well as larval lethality.

Narrative: A cadherin (CDH-1) missense could change cell–cell adhesion properties of AMso, altering cortical cues or mechanical contexts required for asymmetric division and MCM specification [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=31.3; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="cdh-1 encodes a cadherin similar to Dachsous; loss can cause developmental defects."].
rationale: CDH-1 cadherin mediates cell-cell adhesion, which can influence asymmetric division orientation and fate decisions in epithelial/glial lineages.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable calmodulin binding activity and syntaxin-1 binding activity. Involved in regulation of multicellular organismal process; spermatogenesis; and synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Located in presynaptic active zone. Expressed in head neurons; neurons; tail neurons; and ventral nerve cord. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Is an ortholog of human UNC13A (unc-13 homolog A); UNC13B (unc-13 homolog B); and UNC13C (unc-13 homolog C).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: unc-13 encodes at least five protein isoforms that regulate neurotransmitter release by altering the conformation of syntaxin; UNC-13 proteins are required for normal pharyngeal pumping and thrashing in liquid, normally short lifespan, normally large brood sizes, and full adult body sizes; UNC-13 proteins have orthologs in vertebrates and Drosophila; UNC-13 proteins are complex, with multiple C2, phorbol ester-binding, and DUF1041 domains; UNC-13 protein form is localized to most or all synapses; many of the unc-13 mutant alleles with viable phenotypes are transcript-specific, while homozygotes with an unc-13 null (deletion) allele die as paralyzed first-stage larvae.

rationale: UNC-13 regulates neurotransmitter release and synaptic function; while not a canonical polarity factor, neuronal signaling during maturation could influence AMso-to-MCM fate decisions.

MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: gcy-5 encodes a predicted guanylate cyclase with strong similarity to rat atrial natriuretic peptide receptor A; expressed in ASER.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable transmembrane transporter activity. Predicted to be involved in chloride transmembrane transport and sulfate transmembrane transport. Predicted to be located in plasma membrane. Expressed in body wall musculature; excretory cell; hypodermis; intestine; and neurons.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: sulp-1 encodes one of eight C. elegans members of the sulfate permease family of anion transporters; by homology, SULP-1 is predicted to function as an anion transporter that regulates cellular pH and volume via transmembrane movement of electrolytes and fluids; a sulp-1::GFP transcriptional fusion is expressed strongly in several neurons, weakly in hypodermal cells and the intestine, and very faintly in the excretory cell and body wall muscle.
Narrative: A missense in sulp-1, a neuronal sulfate transporter expressed in multiple neurons including amphid neurons, could modify ionic or extracellular signaling environments that regulate AMso behavior and the switch to asymmetric division during sexual maturation [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=8.9; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="sulp-1 expressed strongly in several neurons; predicted anion transporter."]
rationale: SULP-1 is a neuronal sulfate permease strongly expressed in neurons including amphid neurons, so a missense could alter neuronal/glial signaling involved in AMso maturation.

WB_Overview: Predicted to be located in membrane.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: lact-2 encodes a beta-lactamase domain-containing protein that contains a predicted transmembrane domain in its N terminus.
Narrative: A missense in lact-2 (membrane beta-lactamase-domain protein) could potentially alter membrane-associated signaling or processing of extracellular cues in amphid/glial microenvironments, indirectly affecting AMso asymmetric division [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=20.3; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="lact-2 encodes a beta-lactamase domain-containing protein with an N-terminal transmembrane domain."]
rationale: LACT-2 encodes a beta-lactamase domain protein with a transmembrane domain—if expressed in amphid/ glial cells it could impact membrane or secreted cues that instruct asymmetric division.

WB_Overview: Predicted to be a structural constituent of ribosome. Predicted to be involved in translation. Predicted to be located in ribosome. Predicted to be part of mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit. Is an ortholog of human MRPL10 (mitochondrial ribosomal protein L10).
Narrative: A missense in a mitochondrial ribosomal protein (MRPL-10) can compromise mitochondrial function, which often perturbs cell division and differentiation; such bioenergetic or signaling defects could indirectly prevent AMso from executing an asymmetric division to yield MCM [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=37.3; WB_Overview="Predicted part of mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit; involved in translation."]
rationale: MRPL-10 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein; mitochondrial dysfunction can broadly perturb development and cell division asymmetry as an indirect mechanism.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase activity. Predicted to be involved in protein N-linked glycosylation. Predicted to be located in endoplasmic reticulum membrane. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in congenital disorder of glycosylation Il. Is an ortholog of human ALG9 (ALG9 alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase).
Narrative: A synonymous change in algn-9 (alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase) could conceivably affect glycosylation patterns of cell-surface receptors involved in cell–cell signaling that guides AMso asymmetric division, though this is a low-probability indirect mechanism [Effect=synonymous_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; QUAL=38.8; WB_Overview="Predicted to enable alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase activity; involved in N-linked glycosylation."]
rationale: ALGN-9 participates in N-linked glycosylation which can influence cell-surface receptors and signaling; a synonymous variant is low impact but could affect regulation of relevant receptors.
